data.long_meaning: From the Old Norse 'riki' meaning 'ruler' or 'realm'. Rurik was the legendary founder of the Rus' state, also known as Kievan Rus, in the late 9th century. The name Rurik carries the meaning “Ruler of the People” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rurik usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Rurik is an important historical figure in Eastern European history as the founder of the Rus' state, which became a major political and cultural force in the region between the late 9th and the mid-13th centuries. The Rus' state is considered the precursor to the Russian state, and Rurik's legacy has been celebrated in Russian and Ukrainian folklore, literature, and art for centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: In Russian Orthodox tradition, Rurik is considered a saint and is revered as a protector of the Russian people. The story of Rurik's founding of the Rus' state is often seen as a divinely-ordained event, and his rule is seen as the beginning of the Russian people's spiritual journey. Rurik is also believed to have brought Christianity to the Rus' lands, and his rule is seen as marking the beginning of the spread of Christianity in Russia. Rurik is thus remembered not only as a great ruler and founder of a nation, but also as a spiritual leader who brought God's word to his people.
